title: Subjuntivo tras verbos de petición: pedir que, exigir que

sections.content: Verbs of request or demand -- pedir que, exigir que -- always trigger the subjunctive in the clause that follows, since you're naming what someone wants to happen, not reporting a fact. Madero's revolutionary manifesto is built almost entirely from this structure. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: El Plan de San Luis Potosí pedía que el pueblo mexicano se levantara en armas el 20 de noviembre de 1910.
items.english: The Plan de San Luis Potosí called for the Mexican people to rise up in arms on November 20, 1910.

items.spanish: Madero exigía que se anularan las elecciones y que se convocaran nuevos comicios verdaderamente libres.
items.english: Madero demanded that the elections be annulled and that genuinely free new elections be called.

items.spanish: Ante el avance imparable de las fuerzas revolucionarias, Díaz pidió que se negociara su salida del poder.
items.english: Faced with the unstoppable advance of the revolutionary forces, Díaz asked for his departure from power to be negotiated.

items.spanish: El propio Madero pronto exigiría de sus antiguos aliados algo que muchos de ellos no estaban dispuestos a aceptar: paciencia.
items.english: Madero himself would soon demand something from his former allies that many of them weren't willing to accept: patience.

sections.content: Pedía que se levantara / exigía que se anularan: past subjunctive (-ara/-iera) matches an imperfect or preterite main verb, the tense pattern you'll see throughout a historical narrative like this one.
